article.title: How Many Mixers Do You Need Per Person at a Party?
article.body:
How Many Mixers Do You Need Per Person at a Party?

For a four-hour party, plan on about three mixed drinks per spirit drinker, which means three 150ml mixers each, plus around 1kg of ice per guest. Drinks House 247 suggests a 1:3 ratio of spirit to mixer for a highball, so a 50ml measure needs about 150ml of tonic, soda or ginger ale.

Running out of tonic halfway through a party is more common than running out of gin. Mixers are cheap, bulky and easy to forget, and they go flat once opened, so it pays to work the numbers out before you shop. The calculation is simple once you know how many people will drink spirits and how long the party runs.

How many drinks will each guest have?

A widely used planning rule is two drinks per guest in the first hour and one drink per hour after that. For a four-hour party, that is about five drinks per person in total. Not everyone will drink spirits: at a typical mixed party, around a third to a half of guests choose spirit-and-mixer drinks, with the rest on wine, beer or soft drinks.

So for each spirit drinker at a four-hour party, plan on three to four mixed drinks, and round up rather than down.

What ratio of spirit to mixer should you use?

Drink Spirit Mixer Ratio
Gin and tonic50ml gin150ml tonic1:3
Vodka soda50ml vodka150ml soda water1:3
Rum and ginger50ml rum150ml ginger beer or ale1:3
Whisky highball50ml whisky150 to 200ml soda water1:3 to 1:4
Paloma50ml tequila150ml grapefruit soda, plus lime1:3

A 50ml pour is a UK double. If your guests prefer singles (25ml), the same mixer quantity applies; the drinks are simply lighter. A 70cl bottle of spirits gives 14 doubles or 28 singles.

How many mixers for different party sizes?

Spirit drinkers Mixed drinks (4 hours) Mixers needed (150ml each) 70cl spirit bottles (doubles)
1030 to 406 litres3
2060 to 8012 litres5 to 6
40120 to 16024 litres9 to 12
60180 to 24036 litres13 to 18

The mixer column is based on the upper figure plus a margin. Ice is separate: plan about 1kg per guest at the whole party, not just per spirit drinker, because everyone's drinks need it.

Cans, small bottles or large bottles?

Small bottles and cans, usually 150ml to 200ml, are almost always the better buy for a party. Each one is opened for one or two drinks, so nothing goes flat on the table. A one-litre bottle loses its fizz within an hour of opening at room temperature, and half-finished bottles end up poured away. Large bottles only make sense if a bartender is pouring steadily from a cold well.

Which mixers should you buy?

Split your order by the spirits you are serving. A sensible starting split for a mixed party:

  • Tonic water: about 40% of mixers. Include some light tonic for guests who want it.
  • Soda water: about 25%. It works with vodka, whisky and as a spritz topper, and doubles as a soft drink.
  • Ginger beer or ginger ale: about 20%, for rum, vodka and whisky.
  • Cola and lemonade: about 15%, the default for many guests.

Add plenty of still and sparkling water on top. Offering water alongside alcohol is good hosting and helps guests pace themselves.

Garnishes and the rest of the checklist

  • Limes and lemons: about one fruit per four drinks, cut into wedges just before guests arrive.
  • Ice: around 1kg per guest, more in summer or if you are chilling bottles in buckets.
  • Glasses: one highball per guest, plus spares, because people put glasses down and lose them.
  • A bottle opener, a jigger for measuring and a bar spoon.
  • A cold place for mixers. Warm tonic melts ice fast and makes flat, watery drinks.

A practical tip on timing

Chill mixers for at least a few hours before the party, and keep only what you need in the fridge or ice bucket, topping up from a reserve. Cold mixers stay fizzy longer and dilute drinks less. If supplies run low mid-party in London, a top-up delivery typically arrives within 30 to 45 minutes.

Frequently asked questions

How many mixers do I need per person at a party?

Plan on about three 150ml mixers per spirit drinker for a four-hour party, and round up. Small bottles or cans waste less than large bottles.

What is the right ratio of gin to tonic?

A ratio of about 1:3 works well: 50ml of gin to 150ml of tonic. Use more tonic for a lighter drink.

How much ice do I need for a party?

Allow around 1kg of ice per guest, and more in hot weather or if you are chilling bottles in buckets as well as serving drinks.

How many drinks are in a 70cl bottle of spirits?

A 70cl bottle gives 14 doubles of 50ml or 28 singles of 25ml.
